blocks.text: Dear Mr. Jones:

Thank you for the conversations that brought us to this letter, and for the candor with which you and your colleagues described what {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} hopes to find. We are glad to confirm that you have asked Quillon Harbor Advisors to run a buy-side search on your behalf, and because the commercial terms are what your board will read first, we have set them out at the top and described the work after them.
The Terms of Our Engagement

Our fee for the search is {{fact:f:E-2015-001.fee}}. It is a fixed fee covering the whole of the work this letter describes, and it does not depend on whether {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} goes on to complete an acquisition, which we believe is the right arrangement for advice that may, in the end, include a recommendation not to buy.

The engagement will begin on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}, and we expect it to run for about six months from that day, which in our experience is the time a search of this kind needs to travel from a map of the field to offers that {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} is ready to make. If the search leads to a transaction that you would like us to carry through to signing, we would set out that further work and its terms in a separate letter, so that nothing in this one has to be stretched to cover it.
The Search, and the People Who Will Run It

The work begins with a map. We will assemble a universe of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.scope}} drawn from the profile we have discussed with you, independent testing, inspection and calibration businesses that serve manufacturers, and we will screen that universe against criteria that you and your board approve before any company hears from us. The screen will give us a short list, and we will agree with you the order in which its owners are approached.

Alongside the map we will assemble a set of comparable transactions in the sector and in the services around it, so that when an owner first asks what a buyer might pay, your board already has a considered view of what businesses of this kind have changed hands for. That work will be revisited as the conversations teach us more, and we will tell you where the evidence is thin.

Most of the owners we will be calling founded the businesses they run, and few of them have given serious thought to selling, so the first conversation with each of them matters more than any document we will produce. Every approach will be made by telephone by one of our senior people, describing your company in terms you have approved and without your name, and an owner who wishes to go further will sign a confidentiality agreement before learning who our client is or sharing anything of substance about the business. From those conversations we will help you decide which companies merit an offer, and we will support you in framing and delivering each one.

Richard Mccoy, a Director of the firm, will lead the search day to day and will make most of the calls to owners himself; he is the person to telephone about anything of substance. Melissa Jacobson, an Analyst, will build the universe and the company profiles behind it and will keep the record of every contact we make, so that at any point you can see where each company stands. I will read everything that leaves this firm under our name, whether it goes to you or to an owner, and I will remain available to you directly for the length of the engagement.

We will report to you in writing at the natural turning points of the search and by telephone in between. When the field tells us something unwelcome about price, appetite or timing, you will hear it from us early and in plain terms.
Payment and Expenses

We will invoice the fee when the engagement begins, and our invoices are payable on receipt. Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, chiefly travel to meet owners and the cost of any industry data we license for this search, are billed at cost in addition to the fee, and anything material we will agree with you before it is incurred.
Term and Termination

This engagement runs from the start date above for about six months and may be extended by a short letter signed by both of us if the search needs more time. Either of us may end it at any point by written notice to the other; if {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} ends it, the fee already invoiced and the expenses already committed on your behalf remain payable, and nothing further is owed.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} and its plans, and we will use it for this search alone. In any paper that circulates beyond your team and ours, candidate companies will be described by sector and size and not by name, and an owner will learn who our client is only after signing a confidentiality agreement and only with your approval. We ask the same discretion of you in return, since most of the owners we speak with will be discussing a company they have never before offered for sale.
Limitation of Liability

We will carry out the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of an adviser in our position, but the decision whether to pursue, price or complete any acquisition rests with {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} and its board. Our aggregate liability arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid to us under it, except where the law does not permit such a limit, and you agree to indemnify us against claims by third parties arising from the search, other than claims caused by our own negligence or misconduct.
Governing Law

This letter is governed by the laws of the state in which our principal office is located, and any dispute arising under it will be resolved in the courts of that state. If any provision is found unenforceable, the remainder of the letter continues in effect.

If this letter reflects your understanding, please sign both copies and return one to me. Once we have it back, Richard Mccoy will send you a draft of the screening criteria for your board's review, and that approval is the first thing the search will need from you.

To: Richard Mccoy; Heather Delacruz
From: Melissa Jacobson
Re: {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} buy-side search, opening note

This search will be decided on the first phone call. The companies that fit the Morse PLC profile are mostly run by the people who founded them. Few have been approached by a buyer before. Fewer have thought about selling. If our first call sounds like a broker working down a list, the owner says no and does not take a second one. And in a field this small, owners talk to each other, so one bad call can close doors we have not reached yet. That is the risk. The rest of this note follows from it.

So we are going to be slower at the front than usual, on purpose. We screen the whole field before anyone picks up the phone, and the short list goes to James Jones for sign-off before a single owner hears from us. I will write a one-page profile of each owner as well as each company: how long they have run it, whether family works in the business, whether anyone has tried to buy it before. Richard Mccoy makes the calls himself, in an order we agree with the client, and nobody sends a teaser cold. Owners hear what kind of buyer is interested and why their company in particular. They hear the Morse PLC name only after an NDA, and only once James Jones has approved it. I will update the contact log the same day as every call, so no owner hears from us twice by accident. Heather Delacruz has asked to read the call script before the first call goes out, and she will. This will feel slow for the first few weeks, and the client may ask why nobody has been called yet. If they do, the answer is that a careful screen is what gets an owner to take the second call.

The objectives come out of that approach. The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}} and runs about six months. In that time we want a universe of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.scope}} mapped and screened against criteria the Morse PLC board has approved. We want a short list the board has seen company by company. And we want live conversations with the owners on it that are still open when offers come up for discussion. Alongside the map I will pull together a set of comparable transactions, so the client has a view on value before the first owner asks about it, and they will ask. A big contact count is not the target. What we will measure ourselves on is how many owners are still talking to us at that point.

What we need from the client side is decisions more than documents, and we need them early. James Jones has offered to take the screening criteria to his board, and their sign-off lets us finish the screen against something fixed instead of something that moves. We also need a person at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} who can say yes or no on a company within a day or so, because an owner who has agreed to talk should not be left waiting on us. Just as important is his agreement to the wording that describes the buyer on a first call, since for an owner that wording is everything they hear from us before the NDA. Richard Mccoy is seeing him this week and will take all of this along. Shout if I have any of it wrong before then.
Acquisition Search for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}
Briefing for James Jones, Chief Financial Officer, Morse PLC. Prepared by Melissa Jacobson with Richard Mccoy and Heather Delacruz.
Where the Search Stands

items: 1. The search opened on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.start}}. We are in the mapping and screening phase, which is where the plan put us at this point.
2. Our universe stands at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.scope}}, built from trade directories, accreditation listings, industry association rosters and our own files.
3. The screen runs against the criteria your board approved. Those criteria have not changed, and the screen is close to finished.
4. Each company that clears the screen gets a one-page profile of the business and of its owner.
5. No owner has been approached yet. First calls wait on your sign-off of the short list.

blocks.text: What the Field Looks Like

items: 1. The field is fragmented. Most companies are founder-owned and run from one site or a small regional network.
2. Accreditation divides it. Accredited laboratories hold customers longer and carry more recurring calibration work.
3. Few owners have taken outside capital. Most have never run a sale process and will need the process explained.
4. Pricing across {{fact:f:E-2015-001.comparators}} rewards recurring contract revenue over one-off project testing.
5. Regional roll-ups are already active. Some owners on our list will have heard from one, which shapes how we open the call.

blocks.text: From Here to First Calls

items: 1. We finish the screen and send you the short list, company by company, for sign-off.
2. We agree with you the wording that describes the buyer on a first call. It describes a strategic acquirer and does not use the name.
3. Richard Mccoy begins owner calls in the agreed order once the list is approved. Heather Delacruz reads the call script first.
4. Every call is logged the same day, so you can see where each owner stands at any point.
5. Our weekly call continues. A written status report follows at the midpoint of the engagement.

blocks.text: Working Session: {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} Acquisition Search
Present

items: Heather Delacruz, Managing Partner
Richard Mccoy, Director
Melissa Jacobson, Analyst
James Jones, Chief Financial Officer, Morse PLC

blocks.text: Outreach so far

We began with outreach, which Richard Mccoy has been running from the short list since the screen closed at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.pipeline-targets-screened}}, and he gave James Jones a full account of the calls made so far and of how the owners have received them. The accredited laboratories have mostly been willing to keep talking and the general testing businesses have been cooler, and as Rick put it, the owners who have said no have said it politely enough that the door stays open for a later conversation. We agreed to keep the order as it stands and to finish the remaining first calls before anything is added, and James Jones was content that {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} should hold the list where it is until then.

James Jones asked whether any owner had raised price on a first call, and Richard Mccoy said that a couple had asked in passing and had accepted, without any difficulty, that it was too early to say. Melissa Jacobson observed that the owners who want to keep talking have nearly all asked what would become of their staff, and we agreed that whatever we say about the buyer should say something honest on that point as well.
What an owner hears before an NDA

The second topic was what we say to an owner who asks, before signing anything, who the buyer is and what it might pay. James Jones would prefer that owners hear the name early, on the view that it reassures more than it alarms, while Richard Mccoy and I argued for holding it until an NDA is signed, because several of these owners know one another and a name that travels ahead of the agreement cannot be called back. We settled on holding the name, on describing Morse PLC only as a strategic acquirer with a serious interest in the sector, and on declining any discussion of price until an NDA is in place and the owner has shared basic financial information.

James Jones accepted the reasoning, though he asked that we look at it again if an owner of real interest refuses to go further without the name, and we agreed that any such case would come to him and to me before anything is said. Richard Mccoy will keep a note of every owner who asks, so that we can see early whether the question is becoming a pattern across the list.
Carried out of the session

Richard Mccoy carries the remaining first calls and will tell me the same day when an owner asks to meet, and he will keep the note of owners who ask for the buyer's name. Melissa Jacobson will keep the contact log current, bring the owner profiles up to date with what the calls have taught us, and draft a short standard description of the buyer for Richard to use, so that every owner hears the same words.

James Jones will show that description to his board and come back to us with any changes, and I will read it before it is used. The next step is Melissa's draft, which she will send to James Jones before the end of the week.
Status Report: Acquisition Search for {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}}
For James Jones, Chief Financial Officer, Morse PLC. From Melissa Jacobson, with Richard Mccoy and Heather Delacruz.
Since Our Briefing

The search is at its midpoint and on plan. First calls are done, and the first NDA conversations have started. The period opened with the screen. We closed it against the criteria your board approved and sent you the short list, and you signed it off as it stood. Richard Mccoy then began calling owners in the order we agreed, starting with the accredited calibration laboratories and moving on to the general testing businesses. Every owner heard the same description of the buyer: a strategic acquirer with a serious interest in the sector, not named. Every call went into the contact log the same day. When we met earlier this month we agreed to hold the Morse PLC name until an NDA is signed. That has held up well, and owners have not pressed hard for it. The questions they do ask are about people and plans. Will the staff be kept on? Will the company keep its name with its customers? Will the owner be asked to stay, and for how long? Richard has answered these in general terms and told owners that a fuller answer comes after the NDA. Where an owner asked to hear more, he sent our form of NDA with a short covering note, which Heather Delacruz read before it went out. Some owners said no. Most said it politely, and a few asked us to call again later in the year. We have logged those separately so they are not lost. I kept the owner profiles current as each call came in, so the short list now records what each owner told us as well as what the screen found. The last first calls were made this week, which closes the outreach stage on the schedule we set at kickoff.
The Count

The quantities stand as follows. The universe is unchanged at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.scope}}; we have added nothing to it since the criteria were approved. Our valuation work still rests on {{fact:f:E-2015-001.comparators}}, drawn from the sector and its adjacent services. The screen closed at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.pipeline-targets-screened}}. First-call outreach is complete at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.pipeline-targets-contacted}}. Each of these is its own measure, and we report each as it stands. A company counts as contacted only when Richard has spoken with the owner directly. A message left with a receptionist does not count, and neither does a letter. On budget, we are working within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2015-001.fee}} set in the engagement letter, and nothing in the plan ahead changes that. Expenses so far are modest: industry data licensed for the screen and a little travel. We will raise anything material with you before we incur it, as the letter provides.
What Comes Next, and What It Assumes

The next stage is NDAs, then information from the owners who sign, then offers. We expect NDAs to come in over the coming weeks. That expectation rests on three assumptions, and you should see them plainly. The first is that owners now in NDA discussion keep their pace through the summer, when several of them step away from the business for a while. The second is that your board's criteria hold. A change now would send us back to the screen and cost the time the careful start bought us. The third is that {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} can give an owner an indication of value soon after the NDA is signed, because that is the question every owner asks next.

One risk sits outside those assumptions. Several owners told Richard Mccoy that a regional consolidator had been in touch with them this year. None of them described a live offer. But an owner who has been courted once will measure us against that experience, and a slow answer after the NDA would compare badly. That is why the third assumption matters most, and why we would like the board's view on value settled early in the NDA stage.

If the three assumptions hold, we expect to be discussing offers with you in the last weeks of the engagement. If one of them slips, we will tell you which one and what it does to the timetable. The next written report will follow when the NDA stage is complete, and it will carry a short summary of each company that has signed. Before then, Richard Mccoy will call you next week to go through the NDA conversations company by company.
Pre-Offer Review: {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} Acquisition Search
Attending

items: Heather Delacruz (Managing Partner)
Richard Mccoy (Director)
Melissa Jacobson (Analyst)
James Jones (Chief Financial Officer, Morse PLC)

blocks.text: The session

Richard Mccoy opened by taking us back through the search from its beginning, from the screen that closed at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.pipeline-targets-screened}} through the first calls, {{fact:f:E-2015-001.pipeline-targets-contacted}} in all, to the confidentiality agreements now in place, which stand at {{fact:f:E-2015-001.pipeline-ndas-executed}}, and he described what each signed company has shared with us since. James Jones then raised whether {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} should reopen the screen to bring in a few companies that had fallen just outside the criteria, and after some discussion he dropped the idea himself, since any company approached now would trail the others by months and would ask his board to judge a business it had never seen.

Melissa Jacobson went through the information summaries she has prepared on each signed company, and Richard Mccoy set out which of them he would recommend for an indicative offer and why, ending, as he usually does, with the strongest case against his own recommendation. A suggestion that outside accountants be brought in for early diligence on the leading company was raised and set aside, on the view that it is premature until an owner has accepted an offer in principle and that an early visit from accountants would unsettle an owner who has not yet decided to sell.

Before the session closed, Melissa Jacobson raised the owners who had asked earlier in the search to be called again later in the year, and we agreed to leave them be until the offers are out, so that our attention stays where the search now is. James Jones also asked that the papers for his board name the companies under consideration, and because those papers are privileged and go to the directors alone, we agreed that they may, while our own summaries continue to describe each company by sector and size.
Left open

Two questions remain open at the close of the session. The first is the range of value {{fact:f:E-2015-001.client}} is prepared to put in writing, which James Jones will take to his board with Richard Mccoy's valuation summary in hand, and the second is whether the offers go out together or one at a time, on which Richard and I see it differently and which we agreed to settle once the board has given its view.

Richard's view is that offers sent together give each owner the sense of a process with a timetable, and mine is that owners who founded their companies respond better to an approach that is theirs alone, so we will put both cases to James Jones in writing and let the board weigh them alongside the price. Melissa Jacobson will have a draft offer letter for each recommended company ready for James Jones before his board meets, and the next step is his call to Richard Mccoy with the board's answer.
